_comment: Weblate configuration for the Mysterria website. Applied by
scripts/provision_weblate.py. This file is the replacement for crowdin.yml.
THE TRADITIONAL CHINESE GUARD WORKS DIFFERENTLY HERE THAN ON CROWDIN.
On Crowdin the guard was 'never add zh-TW as a target language'. Weblate does
not work that way: it finds translations by globbing filemask against the
repository, and every zh-TW.json is committed. Without language_regex on each
component, Weblate imports them as editable translations, volunteers spend
time on them, and the next run of scripts/build-zh-tw.mjs silently overwrites
that work. The regex is the only thing preventing it. Do not relax it.
Weblate exposes every JSON leaf as translatable, including the structural
'id'). Weblate has no per-key exclusion for JSON, so that check stays the
backstop - see _notes.frozen_fields below for the bulk-edit follow-up.

_notes.linked_repos: Only the 'ui' component names a real git URL. The other four use repo 'weblate://mysterria-website/ui', which makes them share that single clone. Five independent clones of the same repository would otherwise fight each other on push and quintuple the disk and fetch cost.
_notes.file_format: json-nested, not json. The locale files are nested objects; the flat 'json' format would key them as literal dotted strings and lose the structure on write.
_notes.rules_filemask: 'rules_*.json' does not match 'staff_rules_en.json' - the filename has to start with 'rules_' - so the two components do not overlap. Verified, not assumed.
_notes.frozen_fields: check-i18n.mjs freezes rule 'id' and 'severity' and guide topic 'id' because the site keys off them. Weblate will still show them as translatable strings. Follow-up: add the 'Bulk edit' add-on to each component with query 'key:*.id OR key:*.severity' and flag 'read-only', which greys them out in the editor. Until then check-i18n.mjs in CI is what catches an edit.
_notes.vcs: Plain 'git' over SSH, set on the 'ui' component only; the other four inherit it through repo: weblate://mysterria-website/ui. Authentication is a GitHub deploy key held in Weblate's own /app/data/ssh, so no token is stored in Weblate's database and nothing secret appears in this file. The host is the alias 'github-frontend', not github.com: the Weblate container serves two repositories, and its generated ssh wrapper offers both private keys with id_rsa first, so whichever key is valid first wins and locks the connection to that key's repository. The alias exists to pin this repo to id_rsa and CircleOfImagination to id_ed25519 - see the comments in /app/data/ssh/config on the server. Do not change the host here without updating that file.
_notes.vcs_not_github: 'github' (GitHub pull request) is deliberately NOT used, and switching to it will break the component. GithubRepository.format_api_host() maps only the literal host 'github.com' to api.github.com, and get_credentials_by_hostname() then looks the result up in GITHUB_CREDENTIALS, which is keyed 'api.github.com'. Our host is the SSH alias 'github-frontend', so the lookup raises 'GitHub API access for github-frontend is not configured'; and were the key added, format_url() would treat the unknown host as GitHub Enterprise and build https://github-frontend/api/v3/... The alias and the github vcs are mutually exclusive. Checked against the Weblate 2026.8 source in the running container, not assumed.
_notes.push_branch: Load-bearing, and empty on the server at one point, which is what this file was reconciled against. Weblate commits translations to its own clone and then pushes; with push_branch set, GitRepository.push() runs 'git push origin main:weblate-website-ui' instead of pushing to main. Three things hang off that branch name: .github/workflows/weblate-regenerate.yml triggers on it and regenerates Traditional Chinese so the derived files are in the pull request rather than landing after review; the i18n.yml checks (check:zh-tw, check:i18n) get a chance to fail before the change is in main; and a human reviews the result. With push_branch empty, Weblate pushes straight to main and all three are skipped. Because vcs is 'git' and not a merge-request backend, Weblate pushes the branch but does not open the pull request - do that by hand, as with PR #2.
_notes.commit_messages: Deliberately unset. Weblate's project-level conventional-commit defaults are better than anything worth hardcoding and stay current across upgrades.
